Re: Appeal of prior-authorization denial  
Member: Skyler Alvarez  
Member ID: W485219153  
Plan: Cigna Commercial/ACA, South Carolina  
Reference number: POC-8B473A1D50-39674  
Requested service: Arthroscopic rotator cuff repair  
CPT: 29827  
Surgeon: Reyes, MD

To the Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Cigna’s denial dated August 21, 2026, which states that the submitted imaging findings do not support the medical necessity of rotator cuff repair.

The MRI directly demonstrates a structural injury that corresponds to my symptoms and examination findings. On July 13, 2026, MRI showed a full-thickness supraspinatus tear measuring 1.8 cm, with grade 2 fatty atrophy. The tear is not merely an incidental or nonspecific imaging finding. I have had 12 months of progressive shoulder pain despite rest, and I cannot lift my arm above shoulder height or sleep on the affected side. Examination showed positive provocative testing and range of motion limited by pain.

I have also completed substantial conservative treatment without adequate improvement:

- Supervised physical therapy focused on rotator cuff strengthening and scapular mechanics
- Fourteen weeks of therapy from March 25, 2026, through July 1, 2026
- Sixteen completed physical therapy visits, documented in the discharge note
- NSAID treatment for eight months with inadequate relief
- Corticosteroid injection on May 12, 2026, producing only three weeks of partial relief

These records establish persistent, function-limiting symptoms, objective examination abnormalities, MRI-confirmed full-thickness tendon disruption, and failure of prolonged nonsurgical treatment. The imaging also provides clinically relevant information about the tear size and the condition of the rotator cuff muscle. The MRI findings should be reviewed together with the duration of symptoms, functional impairment, examination findings, and failed conservative care rather than considered in isolation.

The patient has no active infection, no untreated substance-use condition, is a nonsmoker, and has a BMI of 29. There is no documented medical circumstance in the submitted summary that would otherwise prevent the requested procedure. The requested CPT code, 29827, corresponds to arthroscopic rotator cuff repair for the documented full-thickness supraspinatus tear.

Please overturn the denial and authorize the requested rotator cuff repair. If Cigna continues to deny authorization, please provide:

1. The precise clinical criterion that was not satisfied;
2. The complete clinical-review criteria applied to CPT 29827;
3. The name and credentials of the reviewing clinician;
4. The specific imaging finding considered insufficient;
5. All clinical records and rationale relied upon in making the determination; and
6. The applicable reconsideration, peer-to-peer review, and external-review procedures.

The publicly available Cigna/EviCore document identified for shoulder arthroscopic and open procedures is CMM-315: Shoulder Surgery - Arthroscopic and Open Procedures, effective March 7, 2026. I request that Cigna identify whether that document, another Cigna policy, or delegated-vendor criteria were applied to this authorization and provide the exact criteria used in this case. I am not quoting the plan’s complete rotator cuff-repair checklist here because the denial notice does not identify the specific checklist or criterion used.

Please treat this as a formal customer appeal of the adverse benefit determination. Please send the appeal decision in writing.

Sincerely,

Skyler Alvarez  
[Mailing address]  
[Telephone number]  
[Email address]

Enclosures:

- Corticosteroid injection record dated May 12, 2026
- Orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation from Reyes, MD
- Any additional medical records supporting the request
